quests.instruction: Which word takes the most taps when you count its sounds?
quests.hint: Count the sounds carefully. Digraphs and tch count as one sound.
quests.explanation: “Stretch” has 5 sounds: /s/ /t/ /r/ /e/ /ch/. “Thrill” and “brush” have 4.

quests.instruction: Which word is made from the chunks “ex” + “plain”?
quests.hint: Blend the chunks, then check the vowel team.
quests.explanation: “Ex” + “plain” makes “explain”, with ai saying long a in the second syllable.
quests.funFact: Explain has the word plain inside it, which sounds just like plane.

quests.instruction: Which word has an /ar/ sound and a soft g?
quests.hint: Find the word that has an r-controlled vowel and a g that says /j/.
quests.explanation: “Large” has /ar/ and a soft g spelled ge. “Lark” has a hard k and “charm” has /ch/.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /th/ /r/ /ō/?
quests.hint: Blend all three sounds, then check the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Throw” is /th/ /r/ /ō/. “Threw” has long oo and “thaw” has /aw/.
quests.funFact: Throw and threw sound different at the end but mean different things: one is now, one is past.

quests.instruction: Which word has /ch/ spelled tch and a short vowel?
quests.hint: Look for the letters tch.
quests.explanation: “Kitchen” has tch for /ch/ after a short vowel. “Chicken” spells /ch/ with ch, and “kitten” has no /ch/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a long vowel but NO silent e or vowel team?
quests.hint: Think about open syllables.
quests.explanation: “Tiger” has an open first syllable, ti-ger, so the i is long. “Tin” has short i and “tire” uses silent e.

quests.instruction: Which word has /oy/ spelled oi and ends with /nt/?
quests.hint: Check both the vowel and the ending.
quests.explanation: “Joint” has oi for /oy/ and ends with /nt/. “Jaunt” has /aw/ and “junk” has short u.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT have a vowel team?
quests.hint: Look for letters that team up in each word.
quests.explanation: “Blanket” has only single vowels. “Raincoat” has ai and oa, and “seesaw” has ee and aw.

quests.instruction: Which word has two different sounds for the letter c?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to each c.
quests.explanation: “Cancel” has a hard c, /k/, then a soft c, /s/. “Cactus” has two hard c sounds, and “candy” has only one c.
quests.funFact: Cancel starts with a hard c and later has a soft c, so one word can use both sounds.

quests.instruction: Which word has the long e sound in the middle and ends with a digraph?
quests.hint: Look for ea and ch.
quests.explanation: “Beach” has ea saying long e and ends with ch. “Bench” has short e and “bash” has short a.
quests.funFact: Beach, teach, reach and peach all use ea followed by ch.

quests.instruction: Which word has /er/ at the end?
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound.
quests.explanation: “Winter” ends with /er/, spelled er. “Wind” ends with /d/ and “willow” ends with long o.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /sh/ sound but is NOT spelled sh?
quests.hint: Look for another way to spell /sh/.
quests.explanation: “Nation” spells /sh/ with ti in -tion. “Ship” and “push” spell it with sh.

quests.instruction: Which word has a long vowel in its second syllable?
quests.hint: Divide each word and check the second syllable.
quests.explanation: “Inside” divides in-side, and the second syllable has long i. “Insect” and “input” have short vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent letter in the middle?
quests.hint: Say each word and notice which letter you do not hear.
quests.explanation: In “listen”, the t is silent. “Lesson” and “lemon” have no silent letters.
quests.funFact: Listen, castle and whistle each have a silent t.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with three consonant sounds in a row?
quests.hint: Count the sounds before the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Scrub” starts with /s/ /k/ /r/. “Scoop” and “scarf” have two sounds before the vowel.

quests.instruction: Which word spells /oy/ with oy?
quests.hint: Look for oy in the word.
quests.explanation: “Royal” spells /oy/ with oy. “Oil” and “coin” use oi.

quests.instruction: Which word has /aw/ spelled au?
quests.hint: Look for a word with au in the middle.
quests.explanation: “Launch” has au for /aw/. “Lawn” has aw and “long” has short o and /ng/.
quests.funFact: Launch, sauce and haul all use au for the /aw/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has a vowel team in the first syllable and an -ing ending?
quests.hint: Look for ai or another team in the first chunk.
quests.explanation: “Raining” has ai in rain and the ending -ing.

quests.instruction: Which word has /er/ spelled ur in the first syllable and ends with -ing?
quests.hint: Look for ur and -ing.
quests.explanation: “Burning” has ur for /er/. “Barking” has /ar/ and “boiling” has /oy/.
quests.funFact: Burning, turning and hurting all use ur plus -ing.

quests.instruction: Which word has the long i sound spelled igh and ends with -ing?
quests.hint: Look for igh in the word.
quests.explanation: “Lighting” has igh. “Hiding” and “riding” use the i_e pattern.

quests.instruction: Which word has the -est ending and a doubled consonant?
quests.hint: Look for -est and a double letter.
quests.explanation: “Biggest” doubles the g and adds -est. “Bigger” uses -er and “best” has no doubled letter.

quests.instruction: Which word has three syllables and both a soft c and a hard c?
quests.hint: Count syllables first, then listen to each c.
quests.explanation: “Bicycle” has three syllables, bi-cy-cle, with a soft c followed by a hard c. “Pencil” and “circus” have two syllables.
quests.funFact: Bicycle starts with bi, which means two. A bicycle has two wheels.

quests.instruction: Which word has three syllables and ends with -tion?
quests.hint: Clap the beats in each word.
quests.explanation: “Invention” has 3 syllables: in-ven-tion. “Station” and “nation” have 2.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent w and a short vowel?
quests.hint: Look for wr and listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Wrong” has a silent w and the short o sound. “Wrote” and “write” have long vowels.

quests.instruction: One word is misspelled. Which one? “The knight rode his horce over the bridge.”
quests.hint: Check how /or/ and the soft /s/ are spelled.
quests.explanation: The correct spelling is “horse”. The final e is silent, and the s still says /s/. The other words are spelled correctly.
quests.funFact: Many English words end with a silent e even when the vowel is not long, like horse and house.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /ow/ sound spelled ow and ends with -ing?
quests.hint: Listen for the /ow/ sound in the first syllable.
quests.explanation: “Growling” has /ow/. “Growing” and “glowing” have long o.

quests.instruction: Tap out the sounds in each word. Which word needs five taps?
quests.hint: Count the sounds and remember that th and er each count once.
quests.explanation: “Thunder” has 5 sounds: /th/ /u/ /n/ /d/ /er/. “Thumb” and “thick” each have 3.

quests.instruction: Here is a made-up word: “flaip”. Which real word has the same vowel pattern?
quests.hint: Look at the vowel letters in flaip, then match them.
quests.explanation: “Flaip” uses ai for long a, just like “rain”. “Rap” has short a and “ripe” has long i.

quests.instruction: Which word has the most beats when you clap it?
quests.hint: Clap each word. Which one has the most claps?
quests.explanation: “Strawberry” has 3 syllables: straw-ber-ry. “Splashing” and “thunder” have 2.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /s/ /t/ /r/ /ā/ /n/ /j/?
quests.hint: Use every sound. The last one is soft g.
quests.explanation: “Strange” has 6 sounds: /s/ /t/ /r/ /ā/ /n/ /j/. “Strain” has no /j/ and “stranger” has an extra syllable.
quests.funFact: Strange follows a rule you know: g says /j/ before e, and the silent e makes the a say its name.
